page: The Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the DLSv5 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable, relying on network-attached storage for persistent volumes.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance across various compute-intensive tasks. The server achieved a strong rating in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16569.0. Memory performance is also robust, with large-block uncached read bandwidth reaching 292.88 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 135.25 GB/sec. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated instructions, including AVX-512 and AES-NI, which is reflected in strong Passmark CPU encryption and extended instruction test results.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is optimized for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It demonstrates strong performance in database operations, software compilation, and static web serving, where it achieved a throughput of 53.15 GB/sec. However, memory-intensive tasks or large-scale LLM text generation represent a tradeoff; text generation for a 70B parameter model is weak at 2.77 tokens/sec due to the lack of GPU acceleration and lower memory density. It is highly suitable for parallel processing, CI/CD pipelines, and web serving.
description: The Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is a compute-focused x86_64 server within the DLSv5 family, powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores and is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, representing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. This virtual machine does not include local storage or integrated GPUs but supports Premium Storage. Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core CPU capabilities, high uncached memory bandwidth, and excellent performance in database operations, software compilation, and static web serving. Conversely, single-core performance and large-scale LLM inference are average to weak. The server is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-dense, parallelizable workloads such as CI/CD pipelines, web serving, and distributed database nodes that do not demand high memory-to-CPU ratios.
